correctness.rationale: The proof classifies arbitrary odd-width boundary-4 states via folded spin columns, yielding exactly two 5n+1 components and n(n-3) isolated states. An explicit order reaches odd threshold five and the disconnected sublevel proves sharpness. Even-width chord-defect accounting proves exactly 2n ground and 4n first excited states; neighbor analysis yields precisely a doubled edge subdivision of C_{2n}. Verified independently by full spin enumeration for all widths 3 to 10 using embedded verifier; infinite claims do not rest on tests.

originality.rationale: Earlier literature already contains the even 2n ground degeneracy and defect count (2022) and width-five Möbius-ladder cutwidth layout (2016); neither is treated as independently new. The distinct contribution is the complete low-defect labeled one-spin transition graph: odd two rooted incidence components plus n(n-3) isolates, and even connected doubled two-subdivision necklace. Exact same-object full texts and actual targeted semantic/literature searches identified no theorem covering those graph structures; inaccessible full material and unindexed Ising dynamics remain risks.

value.rationale: Complete infinite-family low-energy transition topology is a natural physically motivated dynamical invariant, going beyond previously known optimal energy and cutwidth. Odd widths have growing n(n-3) isolated excited states and two disconnected basins through boundary four; even widths have a connected necklace of 2n four-cycles immediately above ground. This precise parity transition matters for single-spin metastability and excitation pathways and is not merely an arbitrary finite slice.
